blocks.x: Despite a couple of major new releases having debuted in theaters and at least two high-profile shows being released on streaming, perhaps the biggest title of this past week was an Apple TV tentpole. The movie in question appears to have been designed as a franchise-starter, and marks Skydance's first release following the firm's takeover of Warner Bros. It was co-produced by Mattel Studios after the blockbuster success of Barbie in 2023, and the underwhelming performance of this year's Masters of the Universe. Unlike the latter film, whose theatrical run proved beneficial for its eventual Prime Video release, the Apple TV movie debuted directly on streaming. Apple hasn't exactly continued releasing movies theatrically, despite the success of Brad Pitt's F1, which grossed more than $630 million worldwide.

The new movie stars John Cena in the role of a secret agent who is framed for stealing a nuclear weapon. To clear his name, he must team up with childhood friends he hasn't spoken to in years and retrieve the weapon from the real thieves. The film also features Jessica Biel, Sam Richardson, and Teyonah Parris. It was directed by Sam Hargrave, who previously made Extraction and Extraction 2 for Netflix. Unlike those action hits, which received largely positive reviews with particular praise for Hargrave's command of action, the new movie is sitting at a 25% score on Rotten Tomatoes.

Four people, four completely different ways of being somebody's family.

Fast & Furious · Universal · Since 2001

Dominic Toretto

You are the head of the table, and you did not ask for the job so
much as end up holding it. Dom is the gravity of this franchise, which is why the films work
best when everybody else is circling around whatever he has decided.

You define family by who shows up rather than by who is related to you, and you would
defend that definition against anybody.

People bring you their problems because you make a decision and then stand behind it,
which is rarer than it sounds.

Your weakness is the same as your strength, since holding everybody together means you
rarely admit when you need holding yourself.

The franchise finale is currently set for April 2027, and after two decades it is still
built on exactly this one idea.

Fast & Furious · Universal · Since 2001

Letty Ortiz

You are the one who says the thing out loud and then does not
take it back. Letty is the least sentimental person at that table and somehow the most
loyal, which is a combination almost nobody manages.

Your friends know exactly where they stand with you, because you have never once
softened something to make a room more comfortable.

You give loyalty rarely and completely, and betraying it is the one thing you would find
genuinely hard to move past.

Letty is the best driver in the family and the franchise keeps quietly proving it,
usually while somebody else is making a speech.

The risk is that people mistake the bluntness for coldness, when it is actually the most
protective thing about you.

2 Fast 2 Furious · Universal · Since 2003

Roman Pearce

You are the reason anybody remembers the night. Roman talks
first, thinks second and is far more frightened than he lets on, which is precisely what
makes him the most human person in the whole family.

You use volume and jokes the way other people use armour, and the people who know you
well worked that out years ago.

Roman gets the biggest laughs in these films and also the best running gag in the
series, which is his absolute certainty that he is invincible.

You would turn up for a friend without hesitating, complain about it the entire time,
and do it again the following week.

The thing worth watching is how rarely you let anybody see the version of you that is
not performing.

2 Fast 2 Furious · Universal · Since 2003

Tej Parker

You are the one who made the plan work while everybody else was
busy being heroic about it. Tej does not need the credit, which is fortunate, because in
this family the credit tends to go to whoever drove fastest.

You are the person who reads the whole thing properly, spots the problem nobody
mentioned, and has already solved it by the time anyone asks.

Tej and Roman are the best double act in the franchise, and it works because one of them
is genuinely competent and the other is genuinely loud.

Your friends take you slightly for granted, mostly because you have made everything you
do look effortless.

You would rather be the reason it worked than the reason everybody is talking, which is
a rare and quietly powerful preference.
